title: Cylinder
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. Draw the first face of the two-dimensional sketch by creating a closed loop. Start with the first line from the origin (0.0, 0.0) to (0.75, 0.0), then draw the second line from (0.75, 0.0) to (0.75, 0.0042), followed by the third line from (0.75, 0.0042) to (0.0, 0.0042), and finally, the fourth line from (0.0, 0.0042) back to the origin. Apply a sketch scale of 0.75 to the two-dimensional sketch. Rotate the sketch using the Euler angles [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] and translate it using the translation vector [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]. Extrude the two-dimensional sketch 0.0277 units along the normal direction without extruding in the opposite direction. Perform a boolean operation to create a new solid body. The resulting cylinder has a length of 0.7499999999999988, a width of 0.004157581580989683, and a height of 0.027717210539931224.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a sketch on the XY plane
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0042) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0042) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create a cylinder
r = r.extrude(0.0277)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0042, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0042, 0.0277) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0277) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
